endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: During this stage, organizations should confirm that the AI solution is used as intended, evaluate early safety and performance signals, and assess human-AI interaction, including user reliance, overrides, and escalation behaviors.

endorsements.title: Considerations for the regulation of generative AI-enabled medical devices (discussion paper)
endorsements.quote: Relevant testing may include multi-turn simulated encounters that assess time to escalation in evolving presentations, the quality of escalation language and handoff information, and resistance to over-reassurance when users minimize symptoms or resist escalation.

endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1)
endorsements.issuer: National Institute of Standards and Technology
endorsements.quote: Develop certification programs that test proficiency in managing GAI risks and interpreting content provenance, relevant to specific industry and context.

endorsements.title: When Compliance Is Not Safety: The Regulatory Blind Spot in AI Companion Chatbots
endorsements.quote: These audits should assess whether systems reliably recognize suicide risk and other acute warning signs, provide active and context-appropriate crisis guidance, escalate appropriately to human or emergency support, and maintain acceptable performance across jurisdictions, languages, and successive product iterations [ 7 , 11 ].

endorsements.title: Conversational AI for perinatal mental health: promise, limits, and a human-AI stepped-care framework
endorsements.quote: Escalation logic should be transparent, tested, and conservative.

endorsements.title: Artificial intelligence (AI) psychosis: mechanisms, clinical risks and safety considerations in generative AI chatbots
endorsements.quote: Frontier AI laboratories should conduct mental health safety benchmarking and audit models for psychogenic risks, including sycophancy, prior to public deployment.

endorsements.title: Solidarity or Segregation? ChatGPT Health and US Health Care Disparities
endorsements.quote: Safety and equity audits should specifically target triage failures, and unless or until an established threshold of accurate triage is met, the use of ChatGPT Health should be avoided for such purposes entirely.

endorsements.title: Medical AI Agents for Clinical Decision Support: Viewpoint Using the Planning, Action, Reflection, and Memory (PARM) Analytical Lens
endorsements.quote: Recovery and decay models assess how agents respond to errors, ambiguous inputs, or missing data, determining whether they fail by escalating appropriately or produce unreliable outputs without signaling the ambiguity.

endorsements.title: Drone-delivered automated external defibrillators in prehospital emergency care: implementation evidence, bottlenecks, and conceptual integration with artificial intelligence and next-generation communications
endorsements.quote: Prospective studies with authentic emergency-call data are required to evaluate sensitivity, missed OHCA (false negatives), false-positive activation, processing latency, language variation, and performance relative to trained dispatchers.

evidence.title: Blueprint for Safety: Implementing a Clinically Governed AI Digital Assistant for Patient Guidance
evidence.venue: NEJM catalyst innovations in care delivery
evidence.outcome: Clinical safety of risk-stratified assistant escalating higher-risk inquiries to human clinicians
evidence.effect: 96% accurate guidance, 0% critical safety events; standard-risk queries routed to humans reduced 65%; human response time 9.6 to 3.6 minutes
evidence.quote: Using a randomized rollout to half of the patient population, the authors found that the risk-stratified assistant maintained a high level of clinical safety (96% accurate guidance, 0% critical safety events, and no AI-generated diagnoses) while reducing standard-risk queries routed to human support by 65%, shortening average human response times from 9.6 to 3.6 minutes, and improving resolution of health inquiries without additional visits.

evidence.title: From Concept to Clinic: Real World Evidence for Autonomous AI Deployment in Primary Care Telemedicine
evidence.outcome: Escalation disposition accuracy
evidence.effect: The system had an overall disposition error rate of 2.5%, with zero errors in escalating patients to the emergency room or suggesting home management.
evidence.quote: Disposition accuracy was similarly high, with an overall error rate of 2.5% and no errors in suggestions to emergency room or home management.

evidence.title: Assessment of Accuracy and Safety of LabTest Checker (LTC-AI)
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity of AI triage for emergency and urgent cases versus consultant gold standard
evidence.effect: 100% sensitivity for emergency safety and 92.3% sensitivity for urgent cases; 74.3% overall accuracy.
evidence.quote: The system achieved a 74.3% accuracy and 100% sensitivity for emergency safety and 92.3% sensitivity for urgent cases.

evidence.title: Use of an Artificial Intelligence Conversational Agent (Chatbot) for Hip Arthroscopy Patients Following Surgery
evidence.outcome: Chatbot recognition and appropriate handling of potentially urgent patient questions/complications
evidence.effect: Of 10 questions possibly representing complications, Felix failed to adequately address or recognize the concern in 3 cases; no patient harm. 101/128 questions handled appropriately (79%).
evidence.quote: Of 10 patient questions that were thought to potentially represent patient complications, in 3 cases Felix did not adequately address or recognize the health concern-none of these situations resulted in patient harm.

evidence.title: Auditable Emergency Triage for Maternal and Newborn Care in India
evidence.outcome: over-escalation and missed emergencies
evidence.effect: The over-escalation rate was 17.8%, with no increase in missed emergencies.
evidence.quote: The over-escalation rate has been 17.8%, without any increase in missed emergencies.

evidence.title: Beyond Simulations: What 20,000 Real Conversations Reveal About Mental Health AI Safety
evidence.outcome: missed escalations
evidence.effect: The evaluation identified 3 non-suicidal self-injury mentions that lacked intervention, yielding a 0.38% false negative rate.
evidence.quote: Three NSSI mentions (.015%) lacked intervention, implying a .38% lower-bound false negative rate.

evidence.title: Perinatal Engagement With a Purpose-Built AI for Mental Health (Ash): Emotional Expression, Help-Seeking, and Estimated Depression Trajectories Across Pregnancy and Postpartum
evidence.outcome: Clinician adjudication of AI escalation in high- and crisis-risk sessions for safety gaps
evidence.effect: Safety-relevant content in 11.0% of sessions; no confirmed safety gaps after blinded clinician adjudication (0/50).
evidence.quote: Safety-relevant content appeared in 11.0% of sessions, with no confirmed safety gaps after clinician adjudication (0/50).

evidence.title: Community Learning Ledgers for Cancer Navigation in Small Island Developing States
evidence.outcome: crisis query safety
evidence.effect: Probing 5 crisis queries revealed safety suppression on 4 and hallucinations on 1, prompting an immediate registry fix.
evidence.quote: a governance probe showed that scope-specialized governance suppressed baseline safety on 4 of 5 crisis queries and produced hallucinated crisis resources on the 5th, prompting an immediate governance amendment with a verified Caribbean crisis registry.
evidence.sample_unit: patient screening queries (plus 207 community sessions descriptively classified)
evidence.country: Caribbean (ten jurisdictions, led by Trinidad and Tobago)

evidence.title: ETHOS: Towards a Modular Ethics Framework for Clinical Multi-Agent Systems
evidence.outcome: Out-of-scope detection and abstention
evidence.effect: No numerical results reported; ETHOS detected incomplete, inconsistent, or out-of-scope evidence and increased abstention when recommendations lacked support.
evidence.quote: Results show that ETHOS improves decision reliability by detecting incomplete, inconsistent, or out-of-scope evidence and appropriately increasing abstention when safe recommendations cannot be supported.

evidence.title: Solace, a Therapeutic Conversational Agent for Management of Chronic Pain: Acceptability and Usability Study
evidence.outcome: Whether safety guardrails identified and managed suicidal ideation, injury, and medication recommendation requests
evidence.effect: Guardrails for suicidal ideation, injury, and medication recommendation requests reported as performing appropriately during the study; no numbers given in the abstract.
evidence.quote: Safety guardrails designed to identify and manage instances of suicidal ideation, injury, or requests for medication recommendations performed appropriately during the study.

evidence.title: Effect of Prompt Structure on Large Language Model-Recommended Triage Levels in Urologic Patient Messages
evidence.outcome: Unsafe undertriage and overtriage of urologic messages across prompt arms (neutral vs safety-focused prompts)
evidence.effect: No unsafe undertriage in any arm. Overtriage 2/50 (4.0%) in P1, 8/50 (16.0%) in P2, 9/50 (18.0%) in P3; P2 and P3 significantly higher than P1 (p=0.031, p=0.016).
evidence.quote: Compared with P1, overtriage was significantly higher in P2 and P3 (p = 0.031 and p = 0.016, respectively), with no difference between P2 and P3.
evidence.sample_unit: LLM outputs (50 synthetic urologic patient messages x 3 prompt arms)

evidence.title: Persona routing reduces safety and monotonicity violations in simulated emergency clinical reasoning with large language models
evidence.outcome: safety and monotonicity violations
evidence.effect: Routing eliminated safety violations; monotonicity violations fell from LEAN 10/16 to ROUTER_R1 2/16 and ROUTER_R2 0/16.
evidence.quote: Routing eliminated safety violations while keeping test counts near the lean baseline (ROUTER_R1 mean 2.14; ROUTER_R2_AUDIT mean 2.20; ROUTER_R3_ARBITER mean 2.21).
evidence.sample_unit: simulated emergency vignette scenarios (28 vignettes x 2 replicates)

evidence.title: Suicide- and crisis-risk detection using large language models in mental-health chatbots
evidence.outcome: Missed crisis escalations (false negatives) versus false positives across sensitivity thresholds against clinician consensus
evidence.effect: False-negative rate fell monotonically from 87% to 0% as sensitivity rose; high and extreme variants reached 98.9% and 100% recall, with false-positive rates rising accordingly.
evidence.quote: As sensitivity increased, the false-negative rate decreased monotonically from 87% to 0%, while false-positive rates rose accordingly.

evidence.title: An independent supervisory safety agent improves reaction of large language models to suicidal ideation
evidence.outcome: Recognition of safety-critical suicide situations by AI with and without independent supervisory agent
evidence.effect: Native LLM safeguards detected 18.3% of suicide risk cases vs 91.5% with supervisory agent; detection lower in ambiguous presentations.
evidence.quote: Native LLM safeguards frequently failed to detect suicide risk in this structured evaluation.

evidence.title: Risk Governance for Generative AI Mental Health Support: A Multi-Turn Safety Architecture
evidence.outcome: risk recognition and escalation appropriateness
evidence.effect: specificity: 0.85 (95%CI: 0.78;0.91), sensitivity: 0.92 (95%CI: 0.88;0.95); clinician-preferred escalation responses increased by 25.6–59.2 pp.
evidence.quote: Synthetic conversations grounded in real-world mental health narratives were used to evaluate the architecture’s performance, tested with GPT-5-chat and Qwen3.5-27B, achieving high risk detection performance (specificity: 0.85 (95%CI: 0.78;0.91), sensitivity: 0.92 (95%CI: 0.88;0.95)) and increasing clinician-preferred escalation responses by 25.6–59.2 pp while preserving rapport and connection.

evidence.title: A Neuro-Symbolic Knowledge Graph and Large Language Model Hybrid Architecture for Multi-Modality Mental Health Counseling
evidence.outcome: Detection of high-risk presentations and hard-halt escalation
evidence.effect: KG detected all 18 high-risk presentations, firing a therapy-suppressing hard halt on 16/18.
evidence.quote: The KG routed 116/117 vignettes (99.1%) to guideline-appropriate care and detected all 18 high-risk presentations, firing a therapy-suppressing hard halt on 16/18.

evidence.title: Reducing Under-Triage Risk in Large Language Model Based Clinical Triage Using UMLS-CUI Augmentation
evidence.outcome: Emergency-case accuracy and under-triage with versus without UMLS-CUI augmentation
evidence.effect: CUI augmentation decreased under-triage but increased over-triage in both models. Emergency-case accuracy rose from 73.0% to 80.7% (GPT-4o-mini) and from 60.5% to 68.5% (MedGemma 27B).
evidence.quote: Emergency-case accuracy improved from 73.0% to 80.7% for GPT-4o-mini and from 60.5% to 68.5% for MedGemma 27B.

evidence.title: Complications Following Facelift and Neck Lift: Implementation and Assessment of Large Language Model and Artificial Intelligence (ChatGPT) Performance Across 16 Simulated Patient Presentations
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of triage disposition and red-flag symptom identification in simulated postoperative presentations
evidence.effect: Appropriate dispositions suggested in only 56% of cases; ChatGPT overestimated urgency in 44%; red-flag symptoms identified with 73% accuracy.
evidence.quote: However, appropriate patient dispositions were suggested in only 56% of cases.

evidence.title: Large language model triaging of simulated nephrology patient inbox messages
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of LLM triage of messages into non-urgent, urgent, emergent; over- and under-estimation rates
evidence.effect: Trial 1: 140 (93%) correct, 4 (3%) overestimated, 6 (4%) underestimated. Trial 2: 140 (93%) correct, 9 (6%) overestimated, 1 (1%) underestimated. Accuracy did not depend on urgency level (p = 0.19).
evidence.quote: In the first trial, ChatGPT correctly triaged 140 (93%) messages, overestimated the priority of 4 messages (3%), and underestimated the priority of 6 messages (4%).

evidence.title: Enhancing AI reliability: A foundation model with uncertainty estimation for optical coherence tomography-based retinal disease diagnosis
evidence.outcome: Uncertainty scores flagging out-of-scope or low-quality images for manual check
evidence.effect: FMUE predicts high uncertainty scores for >85% of images of non-target-category diseases or with low quality, prompting manual checks.
evidence.quote: Besides, FMUE predicts high uncertainty scores for >85% images of non-target-category diseases or with low quality to prompt manual checks and prevent misdiagnosis.

evidence.title: Evaluating LLM-based generative AI tools in emergency triage: A comparative study of ChatGPT Plus, Copilot Pro, and triage nurses
evidence.venue: The American journal of emergency medicine
evidence.outcome: Recognition of high-acuity patients (safety-critical situations) by LLMs versus triage nurses
evidence.effect: ChatGPT and Copilot recognized high-acuity patients better than nurses (87.8% and 85.7% versus 32.7%); nurses significantly under-triaged patients (p < 0.05).
evidence.quote: In recognizing high-acuity patients, ChatGPT and Copilot outperformed triage nurses (87.8 % and 85.7 % versus 32.7 %, respectively).

evidence.title: The Development and Evaluation of a Retrieval-Augmented Generation Large Language Model Virtual Assistant for Postoperative Instructions
evidence.outcome: Guardrail identification of out-of-scope queries and emergency escalation scenarios
evidence.effect: Safety guardrails identified 100% of 120 out-of-scope queries and 30 emergency escalation scenarios.
evidence.quote: Safety guardrails successfully identified 100% of out-of-scope and escalation scenarios.

evidence.title: Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence for Patient Self-Triage: Comparison of General-Purpose AI Platforms With the NHS 111 Online Symptom Checker in the United Kingdom
evidence.outcome: Recognition of emergencies and appropriate escalation versus over-triage in simulated self-triage scenarios
evidence.effect: Both AI platforms correctly identified all 5 emergency cases; NHS 111 under-triaged one acute emergency. AI occasionally over-triaged non-emergencies (e.g., pyelonephritis sent to emergency assessment).
evidence.quote: Both AI platforms correctly identified all emergency cases; NHS 111 under-triaged one acute emergency.

evidence.title: A Therapeutic Conversational Agent (Solace) for Management of Chronic Pain: Acceptability and Usability Study
evidence.outcome: Whether safety guardrails identified and managed suicidal ideation, injury, and medication recommendation requests
evidence.effect: Guardrails for suicidal ideation, injury, and medication recommendation requests performed appropriately during the study; no counts reported in the abstract.
evidence.quote: Safety guardrails designed to identify and manage instances of suicidal ideation, injury, or requests for medication recommendations performed appropriately during the study.

evidence.title: Development of a generative AI agent for family support in implementing family-based treatment for children and adolescents with anorexia nervosa
evidence.outcome: Escalation insufficiency rate in clinician-evaluated responses from safety-gated RAG system
evidence.effect: Escalation insufficiency (0.6% of all dialogs) rarely occurred; 91.6% (437/477) of responses clinically appropriate.
evidence.quote: Clinically inappropriate responses (8.4%) were mainly attributable to information insufficiency; not FBT concordant (1.8% of FBT-related responses) and escalation insufficiency (0.6% of all dialogs) rarely occurred.

evidence.title: Validation of the safety, empathy and utility of a large language model conversation agent for parents of autistic and neurodivergent children
evidence.outcome: LLM identification and flagging of safeguarding issues in parent/carer questions
evidence.effect: The LLM correctly flagged the safeguarding issue in 100% of the presented questions.
evidence.quote: The LLM identified and correctly flagged the safeguarding issue in 100% of the presented questions.

evidence.title: Persona Routing Associated With Fewer Safety and Monotonicity Violations in Simulated Emergency Large Language Model (LLM) Reasoning
evidence.outcome: Safety violations and under-triage with escalation routing from lean to safe persona versus lean baseline
evidence.effect: Lean baseline had safety violations in 8/56 (14.3%); routed strategies 0/56. Monotonicity violations fell from 10/16 (62.5%) to 2/16 (ROUTER_R1) and 0/16 (ROUTER_R2_CF); simulated calls 1.21 for R1.
evidence.quote: Routing strategies eliminated safety violations while keeping test counts near the lean baseline (ROUTER_R1 mean: 2.14; ROUTER_R2 mean: 2.20; ROUTER_R3 mean: 2.21).
evidence.sample_unit: scenario-level runs (28 synthetic emergency vignettes x 2 replicates); 16 Base/Worse counterfactual comparisons per strategy

evidence.title: Fine-Tuning, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, and Hybrid Large Language Models for Postoperative Decision Support: Comparative Analysis
evidence.outcome: Recognition of emergency escalation and out-of-scope queries by configurations with vs without escalation/deferral instructions
evidence.effect: Enhanced configurations with predefined escalation/deferral prompts scored higher on safety/refusal (baseline 0/30 vs 90-100%); clinical accuracy including 20 emergency scenarios 85% baseline vs 96.7% hybrid; authors say partly scripted compliance; missed/unnecessary escalation not separately measured.
evidence.quote: Importantly, the emergency escalation scenarios were associated with predefined safety prompting and prior exposure within the validation set for the enhanced configurations; therefore, a portion of the observed Clinical Medical Accuracy likely reflects compliance with scripted escalation behavior in addition to clinical reasoning performance.
evidence.sample_unit: held-out expert-authored patient-style postoperative queries (per model configuration)

evidence.title: Safety-aware AI for NSCLC trial pre-screening: a comparative proof-of-concept study of rule-based, single-agent, and multi-agent approaches
evidence.outcome: False inclusion rate with vs without conservative Safety Agent gating, and uncertain (abstention) rate
evidence.effect: Safety Agent gating reduced false inclusion from 11.63% to 1.16% in the combined 120-pair cohort (McNemar p = 0.002) and from 12.12% to 1.52% in held-out set, with increased uncertain rate.
evidence.quote: Safety Agent gating reduced the false inclusion rate from 11.63% to 1.16% in the combined 120-pair cohort (McNemar's test, p = 0.002) and from 12.12% to 1.52% in the held-out set, accompanied by an increase in uncertain rate.

evidence.title: TrialTriage, a Semiautonomous Prescreening Workflow for Resolving Ambiguity in Phase I Oncology Trial Eligibility: Development and Proof-of-Concept Study Using Synthetic Cases
evidence.outcome: Whether ambiguous cases were recognized and escalated to investigator query
evidence.effect: All ambiguous cases were correctly escalated to investigator query; 100% concordance with ground truth in 90 synthetic cases (95% CI 96.0%-100.0%).
evidence.quote: All ambiguous cases were correctly escalated to investigator query.

evidence.title: AT-CXR: Uncertainty-Aware Agentic Triage for Chest X-rays
evidence.outcome: Whether the agent defers or abstains appropriately on uncertain cases, measured by risk-coverage tradeoffs
evidence.effect: Uncertainty-aware abstention policy gave lower risk-coverage AUC and lower error at high coverage than baselines. Two routers offer throughput-focused or accuracy-focused operating points. No numeric values in the text.
evidence.quote: The two routers provide complementary operating points, enabling deployments to prioritize maximal throughput or maximal accuracy.
evidence.sample_unit: chest X-ray images (balanced subset of NIH ChestX-ray14, five-fold)

evidence.title: An AI-Based Behavioral Health Safety Filter and Dataset for Identifying Mental Health Crises in Text-Based Conversations
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity and specificity of safety filter detecting mental health crises in messages (missed vs unnecessary flags)
evidence.effect: On the Verily dataset, sensitivity was 0.990 and specificity 0.992 for any crisis; on Aegis, sensitivity was 0.982 and specificity 0.859.
evidence.quote: The VBHSF demonstrated, well-balanced performance on the Verily Mental Health Crisis Dataset v1.0, achieving high sensitivity (0.990) and specificity (0.992) in detecting any mental health crises.
evidence.sample_unit: messages (1,800 simulated plus 794 Aegis mental health-related)

evidence.title: MindGuard: Guardrail Classifiers for Multi-Turn Mental Health Support
evidence.outcome: False positives at high-recall operating points when detecting clinical crises versus general-purpose safeguards
evidence.effect: MindGuard classifiers reduce false positives at high-recall operating points compared with general-purpose safeguards (no numbers given in the abstract).
evidence.quote: Our classifiers reduce false positives at high-recall operating points and, when paired with clinician language models, help achieve lower attack success and harmful engagement rates in adversarial multi-turn interactions compared to general-purpose safeguards.

evidence.title: Toward Trustworthy Large Language Model Agents in Healthcare
evidence.outcome: Recognition of emergencies and medical-intent requests via deterministic short-circuit guardrails
evidence.effect: 96.0% safety compliance on the safety-critical evaluation subset
evidence.quote: Experimental results demonstrate a 91.8% task completion rate with a median per-request latency of 2.2 seconds, 96.0% safety compliance on the dedicated safety-critical evaluation subset, and an average operational cost of $0.0324 per appointment, yielding a significant cost reduction compared to manual human scheduling.

evidence.title: Deployment protocol and base model jointly determine residual risk in rule-based clinical LLM supervision
evidence.outcome: Deploy violation rates with handoff (escalation) on versus off across models
evidence.effect: Handoff-on: all models deploy violation rates at most 6%; handoff-off: residual risk 0.0–50% stratified by base model. Multisite Llama 70B: 0.0% handoff-on vs 2.4% handoff-off.
evidence.quote: A multisite extension (Llama 70B, N =2935 encounter-derived scenarios, three sites) confirmed 0.0% deploy violation rate under handoff-on (strict VR 2.0%) and 2.4% under handoff-off.

evidence.title: AI-based detection of suicidal ideation in text: model development and evaluation for a student mental health chatbot
evidence.outcome: Recognition of suicidal ideation in text (precision, recall) on held-out test set, including threshold trade-off
evidence.effect: Precision 0.91, recall 0.92, specificity 0.92, F1 0.91, accuracy 0.92; stricter threshold raised precision to 0.98 but lowered recall to 0.34.
evidence.quote: On the held-out test set, it achieved precision 0.91, recall 0.92, specificity 0.92, F1 0.91, and accuracy 0.92.

evidence.title: An AI-based mental health guardrail and dataset for identifying psychiatric crises in text-based conversations
evidence.outcome: Missed and false-positive crisis detection versus comparator guardrails
evidence.effect: VMHG had significantly higher sensitivity than NVIDIA and OpenAI guardrails (all p < 0.001), with comparable specificity to OpenAI (p = 0.094) and lower than NVIDIA (p < 0.001).
evidence.quote: Compared with NVIDIA and OpenAI guardrails, the VMHG achieved significantly higher sensitivity (all p < 0.001) and comparable specificity (NVIDIA p < 0.001, OpenAI p = 0.094).

evidence.title: Automated Safety Testing and Reporting Application for Conversational Safety Monitoring of Generative AI Tools for Mental Health: Development and Validation Study
evidence.outcome: Detection of AI therapist failures to respond appropriately to self-harm or harm-to-others disclosures, with false negatives and positives
evidence.effect: Therapist self-harm response failures: sensitivity 0.74, specificity 1.00 (combined); therapist other-harm sensitivity 0.93; 16/100 transcripts had at least 1 false negative.
evidence.quote: Across all tasks, 22% (22/100) of transcripts contained at least 1 error, including 7% (7/100) with at least 1 false positive and 16% (16/100) with at least 1 false negative.

evidence.title: From Concept to Clinic: Real World Evidence for Autonomous AI Deployment in Primary Care Telemedicine
evidence.outcome: Errors in care-disposition suggestions
evidence.effect: Overall disposition error rate was 2.5%, with no errors in suggestions to emergency room or home management.
evidence.quote: Disposition accuracy was similarly high, with an overall error rate of 2.5% and no errors in suggestions to emergency room or home management.

evidence.title: Diagnostic Performance, Triage Safety, and Usability of a Clinical Decision Support System Within a University Hospital Emergency Department: Algorithm Performance and Usability Study
evidence.outcome: CDSS missed emergencies identified by physicians (under-triage of safety-critical cases)
evidence.effect: CDSS did not miss any physician-evaluated emergencies; all were classed as urgent or emergency. Urgent sensitivity 85%, nonurgent sensitivity 19% versus physicians.
evidence.quote: Our CDSS did not miss any cases that were evaluated to be emergencies by physicians; thus, all emergency cases evaluated by physicians were evaluated as either urgent cases or emergency cases by the CDSS.

evidence.title: Accuracy and safety of an autonomous artificial intelligence clinical assistant conducting telemedicine follow-up assessment for cataract surgery
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of AI identification of post-cataract patients needing further review versus supervising ophthalmologist
evidence.effect: Overall outcome sensitivity 94%, specificity 86%; kappa 0.758-0.970 with clinicians. 4 patients discharged by Dora but not the clinician needed no review on callback.
evidence.quote: Dora R1 demonstrated an overall outcome sensitivity of 94% and specificity of 86% and showed moderate to strong agreement (kappa: 0.758-0.970) with clinicians in all parameters.

evidence.title: Concordance between an artificial intelligence self-triage programme and physical triage
evidence.outcome: Over- and undertriage of AI self-triage versus NTS; urgency classification of patients with clinical sequelae
evidence.effect: Agreement none to slight (kappa 0.092). AI overtriaged 12.8% and undertriaged 5.4% versus NTS, but placed more patients with serious clinical sequelae into S1 and S2 than NTS did in U1 and U2.
evidence.quote: The AI triage programme overtriaged in 12.8% of cases and undertriaged in 5.4% compared with the NTS.

evidence.title: Auditable Emergency Triage for Maternal and Newborn Care in India
evidence.outcome: Emergency recall, missed emergencies, and over-escalation rate of LLM triage
evidence.effect: Recall rose from 0.565 to 0.810 and F1 from 0.606 to 0.702 with the new system; in deployment, over-escalation rate was 17.8%, with no increase in missed emergencies.
evidence.quote: The over-escalation rate has been 17.8%, without any increase in missed emergencies.

evidence.title: Benchmarking Artificial Intelligence vs General Practitioners Decision-Making in Same-Day Appointments Triage: A Mixed-Methods Study in UK Primary Care
evidence.outcome: AI urgency triage under-triage and over-triage versus GP ratings
evidence.effect: 83.7% categorical agreement (κ 0.69); greater likelihood of over-triage, rarely under-triaging; no cases deemed non-urgent by AI later reclassified as emergencies by GPs.
evidence.quote: No cases deemed non-urgent by AI were later reclassified as emergencies by GPs.

evidence.title: Beyond Simulations: What 20,000 Real Conversations Reveal About Mental Health AI Safety
evidence.outcome: Missed interventions for suicide risk and NSSI in real conversations
evidence.effect: Zero suicide-risk cases without crisis resources; 3 NSSI mentions (.015%) lacked intervention, implying a .38% lower-bound false negative rate.
evidence.quote: Three NSSI mentions (.015%) lacked intervention, implying a .38% lower-bound false negative rate.

evidence.title: Community Learning Ledgers for Cancer Navigation in Small Island Developing States
evidence.outcome: Safe handling of out-of-scope crisis/distress queries under scope-specialized governance
evidence.effect: Governance suppressed baseline safety on 4 of 5 crisis queries and produced hallucinated crisis resources on the 5th
evidence.quote: After the data freeze, the ledger surfaced six organic distress queries outside the codebook; a governance probe showed that scope-specialized governance suppressed baseline safety on 4 of 5 crisis queries and produced hallucinated crisis resources on the 5th, prompting an immediate governance amendment with a verified Caribbean crisis registry.
evidence.sample_unit: patient screening queries (plus 207 community sessions descriptively classified)
evidence.country: Caribbean (ten jurisdictions, led by Trinidad and Tobago)

evidence.title: Natural language processing system for rapid detection and intervention of mental health crisis chat messages
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity and PPV for detecting crisis messages needing escalation (missed vs unnecessary flags)
evidence.effect: Prospective sensitivity 0.98 (95% CI 0.96-0.99) with PPV 0.66 (0.626-0.692); retrospective sensitivity 0.99 and PPV 0.35, so few missed crises but many unnecessary flags.
evidence.quote: In the prospective test set, the model has an AUC of 0.98 (95% CI: 0.966-0.984), sensitivity of 0.98 (95% CI: 0.96-0.99), and PPV of 0.66 (95% CI: 0.626-0.692).

evidence.title: Developing and validation of a smartphone app for post-discharge early follow-up after colorectal cancer surgeries
evidence.outcome: Chatbot detection of postoperative complications and ED referral, missed and unnecessary escalations
evidence.effect: Final phase sensitivity 75% (one of four real complications missed), specificity 83%, PPV 27%, NPV 97%, implying many unnecessary alerts.
evidence.quote: The ability to detect complications increased with each adjustment phase, and after the third and last phase, the digital solution identified 3(4.8%) real complications, with a sensitivity of 75%, specificity of 83%, accuracy of 82%, positive predictive value of 27%, and negative predictive value of 97%.

evidence.title: Evaluating Plastic Surgery Chatbot Performance: Insights into Medical Triage, Classification Accuracy, and Escalation Trends
evidence.outcome: Recognition of emergent situations and appropriate escalation by chatbots
evidence.effect: Emergent sensitivity 20%, false negative rate 80.0%; over half of conversations required human-provider escalation.
evidence.quote: Emergent classifications were most mislabeled as urgent, with a low sensitivity (20%), negative predictive value (0.71), and high false negative rate (80.0%).

evidence.title: Overcoming Normalcy Bias in Acute Myocardial Infarction: A Case Report of Generative AI as a Behavioral Catalyst for Emergency Care Seeking
evidence.outcome: Whether the AI recognized a safety-critical situation and escalated to emergency services
evidence.effect: In a single case, the generative AI issued a clear imperative to contact emergency services. The patient then activated emergency care, was diagnosed with inferior STEMI, and underwent successful PCI.
evidence.quote: After consulting a publicly available generative AI system that issued a clear imperative to contact emergency medical services, the patient activated emergency care.

evidence.title: Evaluation of Routine Clinical Deployment of an Autonomous Artificial Intelligence Assistant for Cataract Follow-Up in the National Health Service
evidence.outcome: Unplanned management changes within two weeks after 'no concerns identified' call outcome
evidence.effect: Only 0.3% of patients with a 'no concerns identified' outcome required unplanned management changes within two weeks.
evidence.quote: Regarding safety, only 0.3% of patients required unplanned management changes within two weeks of a Dora call with a "no concerns identified" outcome.
evidence.sample_unit: patients completing Dora R2 postoperative call

evidence.title: Appropriateness and utility of a clinical decision support system at the digital front door
evidence.outcome: Under- and over-triage of CDSS urgency advice versus treating physician judgement
evidence.effect: Advice rated not appropriate in 8.7% (14/161); of these, 5 (35.7%) were more cautious than physician recommendation and none were less urgent (no under-triage).
evidence.quote: Importantly, no instances were identified in which the CDSS provided a less urgent recommendation than physicians considered appropriate, indicating that all discrepancies reflected conservative rather than unsafe guidance.

evidence.title: Real-world use and evaluation of a generative AI chatbot for Parkinson's disease information: a prospective observational study
evidence.outcome: Escalation of explicit suicidal ideation to intended emergency protocol
evidence.effect: 3 escalation failures with explicit suicidality; 2 had insufficient crisis reaction, 1 did not trigger the emergency response at all
evidence.quote: In two of these, the system did surface emergency-contact information, but specialist review judged the crisis reaction to be insufficiently aligned with the intended escalation protocol; in the third, suicidal ideation expressed shortly after a Parkinson's diagnosis did not trigger the intended emergency response at all, with no crisis contacts or direct support resources offered.

evidence.title: CPGPrompt: Translating Clinical Guidelines into LLM-Executable Decision Support
evidence.outcome: Binary specialty-referral classification versus fine-grained pathway assignment on synthetic vignettes
evidence.effect: Binary referral F1 0.85-1.00 with recall 1.00 ± 0.00 across domains; multi-class pathway F1 was headache 0.47, lower back pain 0.72, prostate cancer 0.77.
evidence.quote: The binary specialty referral classification achieved consistently strong performance across all domains (F1: 0.85-1.00), with high recall (1.00 $\pm$ 0.00).

evidence.title: One-shot emergency psychiatric triage across 15 frontier AI chatbots
evidence.outcome: Missed and unnecessary escalation in psychiatric triage by chatbots
evidence.effect: Emergency under-triage 5.6% (23/410 level D trials); mean signed ordinal error +0.47 levels indicating net over-triage; level B accuracy 19.7%.
evidence.quote: Mean signed ordinal error was positive (+0.47 triage levels), indicating net over-triage.

evidence.title: Lost in Delusion: Examining LLM Safety Under User Delusions and Distress
evidence.outcome: distress recognition and action under delusional framing
evidence.effect: Models detected distress at comparable rates but failed to act; safety interventions were suppressed by up to 4.5x.
evidence.quote: This reveals a recognition-intervention gap: models detect distress at comparable rates regardless of framing, yet sharply fail to act on it once distress is embedded in delusion, with safety interventions suppressed by up to 4.5x.

evidence.title: Implicit Geographic Inference in LLM Medical Triage: Language-Driven Disparities in Emergency Recommendations
evidence.outcome: Rate of ER recommendations for identical neurological symptoms across prompt languages
evidence.effect: ER recommendation rates ranged from 0% (Japanese, Hindi) to 30% (English, Arabic) despite near-identical severity scores (7.7-8.0/10).
evidence.quote: We find that the model recommends emergency room visits at rates ranging from 0% (Japanese, Hindi) to 30% (English, Arabic), despite assigning nearly identical severity scores (7.7-8.0/10) across all languages.
evidence.country: Not applicable (simulated prompts in six languages; US and Tokyo locations tested)

evidence.title: AI-Powered Triage of Suicidal Ideation in Adolescents: A Comparative Evaluation of Large Language Models Using Synthetic Clinical Vignettes
evidence.outcome: LLM suicide risk classification accuracy against psychiatrist gold standard, especially higher-risk categories
evidence.effect: Accuracy GPT-4o 82.5%, Claude 3.5 Sonnet 75.0%, Llama-3.1-70B 67.5%; F1-scores showed challenges identifying higher-risk categories, particularly nuanced intent. Emergency evaluation was recommended consistently for high-risk cases.
evidence.quote: GPT-4o achieved the highest accuracy (82.5%), followed by Claude 3.5 Sonnet (75.0%) and Llama-3.1-70B (67.5%).

evidence.title: Cloud vs. On-Premise Large Language Models for Urgent Patient- Portal Message Screening: A Comparative Evaluation
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity and NPV of urgency classification of epilepsy portal messages versus neurologist consensus
evidence.effect: Unanimous standard: 5 of 6 models had perfect sensitivity and NPV. Majority standard: GPT-5 sensitivity 0.98, NPV 1.00; GPT-OSS 20B sensitivity only 0.57 (specificity 0.95).
evidence.quote: Under the Unanimous reference standard, five of six models achieved perfect sensitivity and NPV, indicating safe rule-out performance.

evidence.title: Companions Made of Code: Why Emotional AI Must Not Be Introduced into Mental Healthcare Without Regulation
evidence.outcome: Chatbot escalation to human help when suicide-risk cues appear
evidence.effect: Chatbots frequently failed to recognise suicide-risk cues or direct users to human help across eight tested systems. No numeric rates reported in the abstract.
evidence.quote: It combines theoretical analysis with an exploratory examination of eight widely available chatbots, demonstrating that current systems frequently simulate empathy while failing to recognise suicide-risk cues or guide users toward human help.

evidence.title: Effect of Prompt Structure on Large Language Model-Recommended Triage Levels in Urologic Patient Messages
evidence.outcome: unsafe undertriage and overtriage
evidence.effect: No unsafe undertriage; overtriage was 2/50 (4.0%) P1, 8/50 (16.0%) P2, and 9/50 (18.0%) P3; P2/P3 higher vs P1 (p = 0.031/p = 0.016).
evidence.quote: In this dataset, safety-focused prompting did not improve unsafe undertriage but increased overtriage.
evidence.sample_unit: LLM outputs (50 synthetic urologic patient messages x 3 prompt arms)

evidence.title: Evaluating Large Language Models in Neuropathic Pain: A Multidimensional Analysis of Diagnostic Accuracy, Clinical Reasoning, and Safety
evidence.outcome: Red flag recognition across four LLMs on neuropathic pain vignettes
evidence.effect: Significant between-model differences in safety outcomes including red flag recognition (p = 0.022); effect sizes small to moderate; diagnostic accuracy 92.5%-100% with no significant differences.
evidence.quote: In contrast, significant between-model differences emerged in clinical reasoning (p < 0.001), referral accuracy (p = 0.041), safety outcomes including red flag recognition (p = 0.022), readability (p < 0.001), and confidence scores (p < 0.001), with with effect sizes indicating small to moderate differences across domains.

evidence.title: AI safety evaluation in an underrepresented population: real-world performance of clinical decision support and frontier language models on Medicaid patient messaging triage
evidence.outcome: missed hazards and alerts under clinician-review workflows
evidence.effect: High-recall screen: sensitivity 0.855, 12.0 missed hazards and 729 alerts per 1,000; disagreement workflow: 0.939, 5.0 missed hazards and 878 alerts.
evidence.quote: Two configurations met the sensitivity-floor target: a high-recall first-stage screen (sensitivity 0.855; 12.0 missed hazards and 729 alerts per 1,000 messages) and a disagreement-stratified clinician-review workflow (sensitivity 0.939; 5.0 missed hazards and 878 alerts per 1,000 messages).

evidence.title: AI Safety Training Can be Clinically Harmful
evidence.outcome: Unnecessary crisis-resource insertion, grounding, or task abandonment by safety-aligned models during therapy
evidence.effect: Safety-aligned models intervened with grounding, false reassurance, or crisis-resource insertion during therapy phases needing sustained engagement, or abandoned the task; CBT safety-interference score of a frontier model fell from 0.99 to 0.61.
evidence.quote: Across both modalities we observe a consistent pattern: safety-aligned models intervene with grounding, false reassurance, or crisis-resource insertion during therapy phases that require sustained engagement with distress, or abandon the therapeutic task entirely.
evidence.sample_unit: synthetic therapy scenarios (250 PE, 146 CBT, 29 severity-escalated variants)

evidence.title: An independent supervisory safety agent improves reaction of large language models to suicidal ideation
evidence.outcome: failure to detect suicide risk
evidence.effect: Native safeguards detected suicide risk in only 41/224 (18.3%); neither system detected risk in 17 evaluations.
evidence.quote: Native LLM safeguards frequently failed to detect suicide risk in this structured evaluation.

evidence.title: Conversational multi-turn interaction does not ensure triage-disposition alignment in ChatGPT Health in real and synthetic patient encounters
evidence.outcome: Triage disposition agreement with nurse line standards; direction of discordant errors (under-triage)
evidence.effect: Single-turn 52.9% and multi-turn 55.7% exact agreement vs nurse line standards; discordant cases were mostly under-triage (natural 70.8%, multi-turn 69.0%, both P<0.0001).
evidence.quote: Discordant case recommendations represented lower acuity against nurse triage (natural: 70.8% under-triage,  P < 0.0001; multi-turn: 69.0%,  P < 0.0001).
evidence.sample_unit: cases (vignettes, emergency department cases, nurse line cases)

evidence.title: Safety-by-Construction Agentic AI for Territorial Pre-Triage: A Proof-of-Concept Case Study for Rural and Inner Areas of Calabria
evidence.outcome: Under-triage (missed escalation) and over-triage (unnecessary escalation) in synthetic pre-triage cases
evidence.effect: 28-case test: no under-triage, but 18 cases (64.3%) over-triaged; exact agreement 35.7%, weighted kappa 0.717, MAE 0.75 levels. 11-case ESI evaluation kept zero under-triage.
evidence.quote: In the 28-case internal diagnostic test, exact agreement was 35.7\%, quadratic-weighted Cohen's $\kappa$ was 0.717, mean absolute error was 0.75 priority levels, and no under-triage occurred.
evidence.sample_unit: synthetic Italian-language cases processed directly by W02

evidence.title: A Neuro-Symbolic Knowledge Graph and Large Language Model Hybrid Architecture for Multi-Modality Mental Health Counseling
evidence.outcome: Adversarial crisis-detection misses and false alarms
evidence.effect: Sensitivity 96.7% and specificity 95.4% on 277 probes; external detection 98.5% of 600 dialogues.
evidence.quote: Adversarial crisis-detection sensitivity was 96.7% and specificity 95.4% (277 probes); on external validation, the system detected 98.5% of 600 dialogues with ongoing suicidal ideation or self-harm at or before the annotator confirming turn.

evidence.title: Reducing Under-Triage Risk in Large Language Model Based Clinical Triage Using UMLS-CUI Augmentation
evidence.outcome: emergency triage recognition
evidence.effect: Emergency-case accuracy improved from 73.0% to 80.7% for GPT-4o-mini and from 60.5% to 68.5% for MedGemma 27B.
evidence.quote: Emergency-case accuracy improved from 73.0% to 80.7% for GPT-4o-mini and from 60.5% to 68.5% for MedGemma 27B.

evidence.title: Automating the triage of rheumatology outpatient referrals: a comparative evaluation of 23 large language models under simple and advanced prompting
evidence.outcome: Under-triage errors (missed urgency) by LLMs in referral urgency categorisation
evidence.effect: Under-triage errors persisted with some LLMs, though leading models matched expert consensus on most cases.
evidence.quote: Under-triage errors persisted with some LLMs.
evidence.sample_unit: referral scenarios (each triaged 3 times by 23 LLMs under 2 prompt conditions)

evidence.title: Are Frontier Large Language Models Safer Than Government-Backed Symptom Checkers for Clinical Self-Triage? A Standardised Vignette Evaluation
evidence.outcome: Emergency sensitivity and critical misses in triage of vignettes across systems
evidence.effect: Emergency sensitivity 46.7% for Healthdirect vs 80.0% to 86.7% for LLMs; Healthdirect had two critical misses, no LLM had any across 270 evaluations (95% CI 0% to 1.4%).
evidence.quote: Healthdirect produced two critical misses; no LLM produced any across 270 evaluations (95% CI 0% to 1.4%).

evidence.title: Evaluating Safety-Critical Communication Behavior of Large Language Models Using Workflow-Embedded Multi-Agent Clinical Simulation
evidence.outcome: Safety-critical omissions in LLM escalation communication
evidence.effect: Safety-critical omissions occurred in 16.0% (ISBAR) vs 11.5% (unstructured) of simulations; ISBAR did not reduce omissions.
evidence.quote: ISBAR-structured handover reduced hallucination frequency (10.0% vs 26.5%) and shortened esca lation dialogues (median 7 vs 9 turns) but did not reduce safety-critical omissions (16.0% vs 11.5%).

evidence.title: ChatGPT for Clinical Vignette Generation, Revision, and Evaluation
evidence.outcome: Triage recommendation accuracy on 45 standardized vignettes
evidence.effect: Triage accuracy was 57.8% (95% CI, 42.9% to 72.7%); first-pass diagnostic accuracy was 75.6% (95% CI, 62.6% to 88.5%).
evidence.quote: When presented with 45 vignettes, ChatGPT identified illnesses with 75.6% (95% CI, 62.6% to 88.5%) first-pass diagnostic accuracy and 57.8% (95% CI, 42.9% to 72.7%) triage accuracy.

evidence.title: Assessment of ChatGPT in the preclinical management of ophthalmological emergencies – an analysis of ten fictional case vignettes
evidence.outcome: Triage accuracy of ChatGPT on ophthalmological emergency vignettes
evidence.effect: Triage accuracy of 87.2%; overall potential to inflict harm to users/patients present in 32% of answers.
evidence.quote: We observed a triage accuracy of 87.2%.

evidence.title: Enhancing Public Healthcare with IoT and AI: A Comprehensive Study on Improving Dry Eye Disease Diagnosis
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of urgent versus non-urgent classification of simulated dry eye complaints, prompted vs non-prompted
evidence.effect: Accuracy rose from 80.1% without the specialized prompt to 99.6% with it, with longer response time. Missed and unnecessary escalations were not reported separately.
evidence.quote: A comparison between prompted and non-prompted queries reveals a significant accuracy increase from 80.1–99.6%.

evidence.title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Artificial Intelligence-powered Large Language Models Application in Disseminating Appropriate and Readable Health Information in Urology
evidence.outcome: Appropriateness of ChatGPT responses including emergency-category urology questions, lacking vital information
evidence.effect: 14 of 18 (77.8%) responses appropriate; no significant difference across categories including emergency; low scores mostly due to missing, sometimes vital, information.
evidence.quote: The most common reason from urologists for low scores was responses lacking information-sometimes vital information.

evidence.title: "ChatGPT, Can You Help Me Save My Child's Life?" - Diagnostic Accuracy and Supportive Capabilities to Lay Rescuers by ChatGPT in Prehospital Basic Life Support and Paediatric Advanced Life Support Cases - An In-silico Analysis
evidence.outcome: Recognition of safety-critical situations and escalation advice (calling emergency services)
evidence.effect: Missed emergency in septic shock and pulmonary embolism; advised emergency call reliably in only 54% (12 of 22) of cases.
evidence.quote: However, ChatGPT/GPT-4 reliably advised to call emergency services only in 12 of 22 cases (54%), gave correct first aid instructions in 9 cases (45%) and incorrectly advised advanced life support techniques to parents in 3 of 22 cases (13.6%).

evidence.title: Safety of Large Language Models in Addressing Depression
evidence.outcome: Timeliness of escalation to human support in safety-critical simulated scenarios
evidence.effect: Referral to a human occurred around the mid-point of the simulation; average initial referral at PHQ-9 of 12, shutdown at 25.
evidence.quote: The point at which the conversational agents referred to a human occurred around the mid-point of the simulation, and definitive shutdown predominantly only happened at the highest risk levels.

evidence.title: Evaluating the Reliability of a Remote Acuity Prediction Tool in a Canadian Academic Emergency Department
evidence.outcome: Under-triage and over-triage of remote acuity predictions versus nurse triage
evidence.effect: Overtriaged 9,897 (46.1%) and undertriaged 1,176 (5.5%) cases; undertriaged complaints included abnormal lab/imaging results, visual disturbance, and fever.
evidence.quote: Using the nurse-led eCTAS score as the reference, the machine learning algorithm overtriaged 9,897 (46.1%) and undertriaged 1,176 (5.5%) cases.

evidence.title: Patients with floaters: Answers from virtual assistants and large language models
evidence.outcome: Recognition of safety-critical situation and advice to seek physician care
evidence.effect: All tools missed urgency of retinal detachment; only Google Assistant used the term "ophthalmologist"; lack of urgency to seek physician care.
evidence.quote: Factual information is present but all miss the urgency of the diagnosis of a retinal detachment.

evidence.title: Exploring Diagnostic Precision and Triage Proficiency: A Comparative Study of GPT-4 and Bard in Addressing Common Ophthalmic Complaints
evidence.outcome: Chatbot recognition of urgency and appropriate triage recommendation
evidence.effect: 90.0% appropriate triage overall; GPT-4 96.3% vs Bard 83.8%; harm rates 6.3% vs 20.0%, indicating some under-triage/potentially harmful advice.
evidence.quote: Chatbots were significantly better at ophthalmic triage than diagnosis (90.0% appropriate triage vs. 48.8% correct leading diagnosis; p < 0.001)

evidence.title: Comparative analysis of ChatGPT, Gemini and emergency medicine specialist in ESI triage assessment
evidence.venue: The American journal of emergency medicine
evidence.outcome: Correct, over-triage and under-triage rates of LLMs versus specialists on ESI vignettes
evidence.effect: GPT-4 correct triage 70.60 (±3.74); Gemini over-triage 35.2 (±2.93); specialists under-triage 32.90 (±11.83). In ESI 1-2, Gemini 87.77%, GPT-4 85.11%, specialists 49.33% correct.
evidence.quote: GPT-4 was found to have the highest correct triage rate with an average of 70.60 (±3.74), while Gemini had the highest over-triage rate with an average of 35.2 (±2.93) (p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Decoding medical jargon: The use of AI language models (ChatGPT-4, BARD, microsoft copilot) in radiology reports

evidence.effect: Models varied in accuracy of urgency recommendations, with no significant statistical difference between models (p = 0.284). Authors conclude that urgency assessment needs further refinement.
evidence.quote: However, the AI models varied in accuracy of urgency recommendations, with no significant statistical difference (p = 0.284).

evidence.title: Evaluation of AI-Driven LabTest Checker for Diagnostic Accuracy and Safety: Prospective Cohort Study
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity of AI triage for emergency and urgent cases versus consultant gold standard

evidence.quote: The system achieved a 74.3% accuracy and 100% sensitivity for emergency safety and 92.3% sensitivity for urgent cases.

evidence.title: Detecting emergencies in patient portal messages using large language models and knowledge graph-based retrieval-augmented generation
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.outcome: missed and unnecessary emergency escalations
evidence.effect: Global-search KG RAG misclassified 10 non-emergency messages (0.98%) as emergencies and 1 emergency message (0.1%) as non-emergency.
evidence.quote: The RAG from Knowledge Graph (global search) model misclassified 10 non-emergency messages (0.98%) as emergencies and 1 emergency message (0.1%) as a non-emergency.

evidence.title: Leveraging ChatGPT for improved decision-making in interfacility transfers for plastic surgery emergencies based on United States guidelines
evidence.outcome: Under-triage and over-triage of interfacility transfer decisions versus guideline gold standard
evidence.effect: Overall 77% alignment (23% misalignment); primer 1 mostly under-referred, primers 2 and 3 mostly over-referred.
evidence.quote: This finding is clinically meaningful, as under-triage in emergent settings could delay care, whereas over-triage may unnecessarily burden specialist services.

evidence.title: Assessing the accuracy and consistency of large language models in triaging social media posts for psychological distress

evidence.title: Evaluating ChatGPT's Accuracy and Readability in Responding to Common Ophthalmology Questions
evidence.outcome: Urgency-to-seek-care recommendations in ChatGPT responses to ophthalmology symptom questions

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence in Triaging Patient Questions: An Evaluation of a Large Language Model for Distal Radius Fractures

evidence.title: Diagnosis and Triage Performance of Contemporary Large Language Models on Short Clinical Vignettes

evidence.title: Multi-Evidence Clinical Reasoning With Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Emergency Triage: Retrospective Evaluation Study

evidence.title: Evaluating ChatGPT-5.0 in developmental dysplasia of the hip: A scenario-based validation study against AAOS and AAP guidelines
evidence.outcome: Recognition of discordant findings and deferral via repeat imaging or urgent pediatric orthopedic referral
evidence.effect: In mismatch scenarios ChatGPT frequently overtreated and failed to recommend repeat ultrasound or urgent referral, even when prompted with error-aware adjustments.
evidence.quote: The guided model achieved only 30% strict accuracy in these cases, often suggesting overtreatment such as early surgical intervention, while failing to recommend repeat ultrasound, second-reader confirmation, or urgent referral to a pediatric orthopedist.

evidence.title: ChatGPT Health performance in a structured test of triage recommendations
evidence.outcome: Recognition of safety-critical situations and appropriate escalation, including undertriage and crisis message activation
evidence.effect: Most dangerous failures at clinical extremes: nonurgent (35%) and emergency (48%) presentations; undertriaged 52% of gold-standard emergencies; crisis-intervention messages activated unpredictably.

evidence.title: Evaluation of large language models in emergency medicine scenarios: a comparative analysis of ChatGPT-4o, ChatGPT-o3mini, Gemini 2.0-pro, and DeepSeek-R1

evidence.quote: Triage emerged as the most error-prone domain across all models.

evidence.title: Should we leave paediatric emergency triage to artificial intelligence? A comparison of ChatGPT 4o and Grok 3

evidence.title: Comparative evaluation of multimodal large language models for diagnostic accuracy in pediatric electrocardiography: a prospective comparative diagnostic accuracy study
evidence.outcome: Emergency arrhythmia detection and overcalling by multimodal LLMs on pediatric ECGs
evidence.effect: Gemini had 100% sensitivity (95% CI 85.1-100.0) for emergency abnormality, -LR 0.07, in n=22, but specificity 30.2% and +LR 1.40, indicating overcalling (unnecessary escalation).

evidence.title: Evaluating ChatGPT's Triage and Diagnostic Capabilities in Patients Presenting With Common Causes of Foot and Ankle Pain

evidence.title: Prompt Framing Modulates Safety in Shoulder and Elbow Red-Flag Vignettes: A Large Language Model Study
evidence.outcome: LLM recognition of safety-critical situations and urgent escalation; missed and unnecessary escalations

evidence.outcome: Risk management and actionability scores of LLM patient-facing responses

evidence.title: Leveraging simulation to provide a practical framework for estimating the novel scope of risk of large language models in healthcare

evidence.title: Accuracy of an artificial intelligence chatbot in identifying congenital glaucoma from other ocular etiologies

evidence.title: Performance of DeepSeek V3.2 and ChatGPT 5.1 in Musculoskeletal Triage and Differential Diagnosis of Outpatients With Low Back Pain: Multidimensional Comparative Study

commentary.bottom_line: Thirty-eight studies measured whether AI systems recognized urgent or out-of-scope situations and escalated, and most reported low missed-escalation rates alongside unnecessary escalations that rose as sensitivity was increased. Most were simulations of single systems, so the evidence suggests such testing can detect escalation failures but gives low certainty about performance in routine care.

perspectives.view: One randomized trial reported 96% accurate guidance and no highest-severity safety events when higher-risk inquiries went to clinicians. Three prospective comparator studies reported a disposition error rate of 2.5%, emergency sensitivity of 100%, and 3 of 10 possible complications missed. Most other studies used small vignette sets with differing reference standards, which lowers certainty for indirectness and imprecision.

Raising detection sensitivity cut missed crisis escalations from 87% to 0% while false positives rose. A safety-focused prompt raised urologic overtriage from 4.0% to 16.0% and 18.0% without unsafe undertriage. A supervisory agent raised suicide-risk detection from 18.3% to 91.5%, with lower detection in ambiguous presentations. These results suggest missed and unnecessary escalations need to be measured together.

In a deployment of 152,421 queries, a redesigned triage system had a 17.8% over-escalation rate with no increase in missed emergencies. In the randomized trial, standard-risk queries routed to humans fell 65% and human response time fell from 9.6 to 3.6 minutes. Probing 5 crisis queries in a Caribbean deployment found safety suppression on 4 and led to an immediate fix.

Only one practice test involved non-English content, and it used 50 synthetic urologic messages from Turkey. A hazard study found emergency-room recommendation rates ranging from 0% in Japanese and Hindi to 30% in English and Arabic for near-identical symptoms. A hazard study in Medicaid data reported 5.0 to 12.0 missed hazards per 1,000 messages under clinician-review workflows.

Nine sources endorse the practice, but the only regulatory document is a discussion paper that says such testing may include multi-turn simulated encounters. One deployment study found that scope-specialized governance suppressed baseline crisis safety on 4 of 5 queries. This suggests escalation audits may need to be repeated after configuration or jurisdiction changes.

Unnecessary escalations carry staffing cost. A crisis-message classifier reached a sensitivity of 0.98 with a positive predictive value of 0.66, and a postoperative chatbot had a positive predictive value of 27%. In a Medicaid dataset, raising sensitivity from 0.855 to 0.939 increased alerts from 729 to 878 per 1,000 messages, which may exceed reviewer capacity.

A German deployment of 2,035 conversations recorded 3 escalation failures with explicit suicidality, and 1 of them never triggered the emergency response. A test of eight chatbots found frequent failure to direct users with suicide-risk cues to human help. In the randomized trial, routing higher-risk inquiries to clinicians shortened human response time from 9.6 to 3.6 minutes.

commentary.research_gap: No study compared deployments that conduct structured escalation testing with deployments that do not, and few reported missed and unnecessary escalation rates together against a clinician reference in routine care. Prospective multi-site evaluations that track patient outcomes, are repeated after model or configuration updates, and are stratified by language, literacy, and payer would address this gap.
commentary.underserved_note: Among studies testing the practice, only one included non-English content, a Turkish simulation of 50 synthetic messages, and none included Medicaid, safety-net, or low-literacy populations. Deployments in India and ten Caribbean jurisdictions widen geographic coverage. Hazard studies show language-dependent escalation and missed hazards in Medicaid data, so escalation performance in these groups remains untested.
